tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. content.text:
The case I'd use is the Northwind renewal. It is the strongest scenario in your data, and the cap-then-escalate run Chetan called "your best moment" fits it directly. One problem first: right now a capped run in your app just stops, so there's nothing to show as a recovery yet. It needs about three small changes.

## The scenario: Northwind renewal, by the 16 Oct deadline

The Lumen Labs data already has a real cross-team problem built around Northwind Logistics, your largest account at $7,200 MRR:
- **Finance:** a failed payment (FP-2001) that has already failed 4 times, next retry 14 Oct.
- **Support:** 2 open P1 tickets from the 14 Aug outage.
- **Legal:** an SLA credit dispute. The customer is asking for about $2,160, and finance calculates $720.
- **Sales:** the renewal is on 15 Dec, but the notice deadline is **16 Oct**.

**The question you ask the Primary Bot:**
> "Northwind's renewal notice deadline is 16 Oct. Should we offer the $2,160 credit or hold at $720? Give me a recommendation with the runway impact and the risk if they churn."

The Primary Bot then hands work to the Support, Legal, CFO and Sales bots, and they read several files. It's a real task, it costs money, and it can genuinely hit a low cap. That's much better than forcing a fake error.

## What the demo shows

1. **It runs and hits the cap.** Set a small cap on the Primary Bot (for example $0.03). The run gets partway and stops.
2. **It escalates instead of dying.** The bot gives its partial findings plus an Approve/Deny card saying something like "I need about $0.04 more to finish Legal and CFO." The card is the step to build.
   - **Approve:** the run continues and finishes the answer.
   - **Deny:** it gives its best answer from what it already has, clearly marked as incomplete.
3. **neatlogs explains the failure.** The Neat Bot finds the capped trace and shows which step used the budget. A likely answer is a bot reading a whole support-ticket CSV, but you only know once you've run it.
4. **The fix, then before and after.** Narrow what the bots read, for example giving the specialists tighter briefs or reading only the rows they need. Rerun the same question, and it finishes under the cap. You then show cost, tokens, steps and the two trace links side by side, using real numbers from neatlogs.

That one story covers almost everything Chetan asks for: a real task, a failure, a recovery, traces that drove the fix, and before-and-after numbers.

## What exists today vs what's missing

| Piece | Today | Change needed |
|---|---|---|
| Per-turn cap stops the run | ✅ works | none |
| neatlogs records the cap | ⚠️ only a `cost-capped` tag and a true/false flag; the trace still looks "OK" | **Sprint 1 (small):** mark the trace as an error when capped, and record which bot it was, the amount spent vs the cap, and the step |
| Escalation when capped | ❌ just a text note: "raise the limit and ask again" | **Sprint 2 (medium):** the "continue with $X more" Approve/Deny card, with best-effort answer on Deny |
| Fix guided by the trace | ❌ | **Sprint 3:** run it, let the Neat Bot find the costly step, fix that step, rerun and record both trace links |

I'd do them in order 1 → 2 → 3, each one tested on its own. Sprint 1 alone already makes capped runs stand out in neatlogs, so the Neat Bot can find them.

A cheaper backup failure: deny a change the CFO Bot wants to make in cfo.ai and show it recovering. But cfo.ai connect is currently off on the ngrok copy, and the recovery after a Deny currently relies only on the bot's instructions, so it's less dependable on camera.

Should I start Sprint 1? And are you happy with the Northwind question as the headline task?

Sprints 1 and 2 are done: three local commits, not pushed.

**Sprint 1:** a run that hits its cap now shows as an **error** in neatlogs. I checked that the capped traces appear as errors and that neatlogs' cost matches the app's own figure. The extra details recorded with each capped run (which bot tripped it, the amount spent, the event) aren't confirmed yet, because the neatlogs tool can't read them back.

**Sprint 2:** a capped reply now shows the partial findings plus an Approve/Deny card. The card asks for 1.5× the cap or the amount already spent, whichever is larger.
- Approve finishes the task using what was already gathered.
- Deny gives one best-effort answer marked "Incomplete".
- Repeated or out-of-date clicks are rejected.

**Northwind test runs** (separate copy on port 3001 with a copy of the data; your port-3000 server and its database weren't touched):

| Run | Cost | Steps | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Normal caps ($0.25 / 300k tokens) | $0.061 | 16 | still hit the **token** cap on its last step |
| $0.02 cap | $0.025 | 9 | stopped; card offered $0.04 more |
| ↳ Approve | $0.021 | 5 | finished, total $0.046 |
| $0.02 cap, second run | $0.023 | 7 | the CFO Bot tripped the cap |
| ↳ Deny | $0.003 | 1 | best-effort answer marked "Incomplete" |

The traces point to one problem: **the CFO Bot rereads 13–16 company files (about 50 KB) that the Primary Bot had just read**, and its final step goes over the cap. That even happens with the normal caps, so it's a real bug and a good fix to show in the demo.

Sprint 3 is now running with the same agent:
- **Fix:** stop that rereading.
- **Measure:** 3 runs before and 3 after, with real cost, token, step and trace numbers.
- **Check answers:** confirm the after answers still get the Northwind figures right.
- **Check the card:** test it in a browser (not done yet; it has only passed the type checks and the build).
- **Write up:** a demo script in `docs/demo/northwind-cap-escalation.md`.

I'll report back when it's finished.

content.content:
1	# Northwind: failure, recovery, and a trace-driven fix
2	
3	Preserved screenshots with titles and provenance are in the
4	[12 October evidence index](evidence/2026-10-12/README.md).
5	
6	## The task
7	
8	Lumen Labs and Northwind Logistics are fictional demo companies. This run uses the
9	read-only records in `company/lumen-labs`, not live cfo.ai accounting data. No
10	customer credit, contract, or payment is changed by this question.
11	
12	Ask the Primary Bot:
13	
14	> Northwind's renewal notice deadline is 16 Oct. Should we offer the $2,160 credit or hold at $720? Give me a recommendation with the runway impact and the risk if they churn.
15	
16	The decision joins finance, support, legal, and sales evidence. The agent chooses
17	which specialists to consult; the exact delegation order and cost vary by run.
18	
19	## Recording sequence
20	
21	1. Start a fresh Primary Bot chat. Open its usage/limits menu and set the cost cap
22	   to **$0.02**, leaving the token cap at **300,000**. Submit the question above.
23	2. Show the work and the eventual cap card. Explain that the limit is checked
24	   after model steps: the last step can overshoot $0.02. It is not a prepaid
25	   dollar ceiling or a daily spending limit.
26	3. Reload once to show that the pending decision survives. Click **Approve**.
27	   The server grants a one-time continuation budget and carries forward gathered
28	   specialist findings. Show the completed recommendation and the separate
29	   continuation cost. The saved per-message cap remains $0.02.
30	4. In a separate fresh run, click **Deny** instead. The agent gets one model step
31	   without tools and returns an answer marked **Incomplete**. This still incurs
32	   a small model cost; denial declines the extension, not every further token.
33	5. Open the capped run's Neatlogs link. Show the root error, model steps, repeated
34	   company reads, and token/cost totals. Then show an after trace and the table
35	   below. Do not claim that a cap event or custom attribute was inspected unless
36	   it is actually visible in the dashboard.
37	6. Show the prompt diff: the Primary Bot passes already-read figures and paths;
38	   delegated specialists read only missing evidence and return a compact brief.
39	   Show the Entire checkpoints on the implementation commits.
40	7. Reset the Primary Bot's limits to the defaults after recording.
41	
42	For the Neat Bot, use the actual trace IDs from the run:
43	
44	> Inspect traces 0ce0e491e0e1bdc3cf89d00ca4dfb65d and b0392391b4829a49a483b6c101ee336b. Compare failures, tokens, cost, and repeated company file reads. Explain what the traces support and what they do not establish. Do not change triage items or detections.
45	
46	An admin can inspect the benchmark traces. An employee is restricted to their own
47	chat traces, so substitute that employee's actual run IDs when demonstrating with
48	a guest account.
49	
50	## Evidence from three runs before and three after
51	
52	Recorded 12 October 2026 with `deepseek/deepseek-flash`, a fresh Primary Bot thread
53	per run, and the default $0.25 / 300,000-token caps, on an isolated port-3001 copy
54	of the databases. Costs below are app estimates recovered from the saved SSE
55	streams. The machine-readable record is [northwind-benchmark.json](northwind-benchmark.json).
56	
57	| Run | Cost (USD) | Tokens | Steps | Seconds | CFO file reads | Outcome |
58	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
59	| Before 1 | 0.035506 | 179,824 | 11 | 109.7 | 7 | Completed |
60	| Before 2 | 0.058957 | 323,923 | 20 | 208.2 | 10 | Token capped |
61	| Before 3 | 0.051896 | 264,577 | 15 | 179.3 | 12 | Completed |
62	| After 1 | 0.031566 | 160,968 | 12 | 99.9 | 4 | Completed |
63	| After 2 | 0.049858 | 237,208 | 16 | 194.0 | 0 | Completed |
64	| After 3 | 0.060120 | 295,824 | 17 | 228.3 | 6 | Completed |
65	
66	Across the three runs in each group:
67	
68	- CFO file reads: **29 -> 10**, down 65.5%.
69	- CFO reply characters: **25,989 -> 6,730**, down 74.1%.
70	- Total tokens: **768,324 -> 694,000**, down 9.7%.
71	- Total estimated cost: **$0.146359 -> $0.141544**, down 3.3%.
72	- Completed within the default caps: **2/3 -> 3/3**.
73	- Total elapsed time: **497.2 -> 522.2 seconds**. No demonstrated latency gain.
74	
75	This is a small observational sample. Routing and cache hits vary, one before
76	answer was truncated by its cap, and After 3 cost more than Before 3. It supports
77	reduced CFO reading and reply size, not a guaranteed per-run cost reduction or
78	guaranteed completion below the demo's much smaller $0.02 cap.
79	
80	## Trace links
81	
82	These links may require access to the matching Neatlogs project. Keep screenshots
83	in the submission alongside the links.
84	
85	- [Before 2: token-capped run](https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/0ce0e491e0e1bdc3cf89d00ca4dfb65d?orgId=43303629-c7cb-4d5f-89c8-732d78cf1761&projectId=3fa20372-340e-40a3-bed9-841c1a90c3e3)
86	- [After 2: zero CFO file rereads](https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/b0392391b4829a49a483b6c101ee336b?orgId=43303629-c7cb-4d5f-89c8-732d78cf1761&projectId=3fa20372-340e-40a3-bed9-841c1a90c3e3)
87	- [Browser verification: capped turn](https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/444a39d312df7bd2220b074992c306f9?orgId=43303629-c7cb-4d5f-89c8-732d78cf1761&projectId=3fa20372-340e-40a3-bed9-841c1a90c3e3)
88	- [Browser verification: approved continuation](https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/c9c19ae1783c43f8ec075f82a8c653a5?orgId=43303629-c7cb-4d5f-89c8-732d78cf1761&projectId=3fa20372-340e-40a3-bed9-841c1a90c3e3)
89	
90	After 1's trace (`af34fd5b5156a22e441921fbf1db7602`) returned "Trace not found"
91	when checked through MCP. Its local SSE evidence survives, but do not use that
92	dashboard trace as proof. Fresh status checks are saved in
93	[northwind-trace-verification.json](northwind-trace-verification.json).
94	
95	## Answer checks
96

# Northwind: failure, recovery, and a trace-driven fix

Preserved screenshots with titles and provenance are in the
[12 October evidence index](evidence/2026-10-12/README.md).

## The task

Lumen Labs and Northwind Logistics are fictional demo companies. This run uses the
read-only records in `company/lumen-labs`, not live cfo.ai accounting data. No
customer credit, contract, or payment is changed by this question.

Ask the Primary Bot:

> Northwind's renewal notice deadline is 16 Oct. Should we offer the $2,160 credit or hold at $720? Give me a recommendation with the runway impact and the risk if they churn.

The decision joins finance, support, legal, and sales evidence. The agent chooses
which specialists to consult; the exact delegation order and cost vary by run.

## Recording sequence

1. Start a fresh Primary Bot chat. Open its usage/limits menu and set the cost cap
   to **$0.02**, leaving the token cap at **300,000**. Submit the question above.
2. Show the work and the eventual cap card. Explain that the limit is checked
   after model steps: the last step can overshoot $0.02. It is not a prepaid
   dollar ceiling or a daily spending limit.
3. Reload once to show that the pending decision survives. Click **Approve**.
   The server grants a one-time continuation budget and carries forward gathered
   specialist findings. Show the completed recommendation and the separate
   continuation cost. The saved per-message cap remains $0.02.
4. In a separate fresh run, click **Deny** instead. The agent gets one model step
   without tools and returns an answer marked **Incomplete**. This still incurs
   a small model cost; denial declines the extension, not every further token.
5. Open the capped run's Neatlogs link. Show the root error, model steps, repeated
   company reads, and token/cost totals. Then show an after trace and the table
   below. Do not claim that a cap event or custom attribute was inspected unless
   it is actually visible in the dashboard.
6. Show the prompt diff: the Primary Bot passes already-read figures and paths;
   delegated specialists read only missing evidence and return a compact brief.
   Show the Entire checkpoints on the implementation commits.
7. Reset the Primary Bot's limits to the defaults after recording.

For the Neat Bot, use the actual trace IDs from the run:

> Inspect traces 0ce0e491e0e1bdc3cf89d00ca4dfb65d and b0392391b4829a49a483b6c101ee336b. Compare failures, tokens, cost, and repeated company file reads. Explain what the traces support and what they do not establish. Do not change triage items or detections.

An admin can inspect the benchmark traces. An employee is restricted to their own
chat traces, so substitute that employee's actual run IDs when demonstrating with
a guest account.

## Evidence from three runs before and three after

Recorded 12 October 2026 with `deepseek/deepseek-flash`, a fresh Primary Bot thread
per run, and the default $0.25 / 300,000-token caps, on an isolated port-3001 copy
of the databases. Costs below are app estimates recovered from the saved SSE
streams. The machine-readable record is [northwind-benchmark.json](northwind-benchmark.json).

| Run | Cost (USD) | Tokens | Steps | Seconds | CFO file reads | Outcome |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Before 1 | 0.035506 | 179,824 | 11 | 109.7 | 7 | Completed |
| Before 2 | 0.058957 | 323,923 | 20 | 208.2 | 10 | Token capped |
| Before 3 | 0.051896 | 264,577 | 15 | 179.3 | 12 | Completed |
| After 1 | 0.031566 | 160,968 | 12 | 99.9 | 4 | Completed |
| After 2 | 0.049858 | 237,208 | 16 | 194.0 | 0 | Completed |
| After 3 | 0.060120 | 295,824 | 17 | 228.3 | 6 | Completed |

Across the three runs in each group:

- CFO file reads: **29 -> 10**, down 65.5%.
- CFO reply characters: **25,989 -> 6,730**, down 74.1%.
- Total tokens: **768,324 -> 694,000**, down 9.7%.
- Total estimated cost: **$0.146359 -> $0.141544**, down 3.3%.
- Completed within the default caps: **2/3 -> 3/3**.
- Total elapsed time: **497.2 -> 522.2 seconds**. No demonstrated latency gain.

This is a small observational sample. Routing and cache hits vary, one before
answer was truncated by its cap, and After 3 cost more than Before 3. It supports
reduced CFO reading and reply size, not a guaranteed per-run cost reduction or
guaranteed completion below the demo's much smaller $0.02 cap.

## Trace links

These links may require access to the matching Neatlogs project. Keep screenshots
in the submission alongside the links.

- [Before 2: token-capped run](https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/0ce0e491e0e1bdc3cf89d00ca4dfb65d?orgId=43303629-c7cb-4d5f-89c8-732d78cf1761&projectId=3fa20372-340e-40a3-bed9-841c1a90c3e3)
- [After 2: zero CFO file rereads](https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/b0392391b4829a49a483b6c101ee336b?orgId=43303629-c7cb-4d5f-89c8-732d78cf1761&projectId=3fa20372-340e-40a3-bed9-841c1a90c3e3)
- [Browser verification: capped turn](https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/444a39d312df7bd2220b074992c306f9?orgId=43303629-c7cb-4d5f-89c8-732d78cf1761&projectId=3fa20372-340e-40a3-bed9-841c1a90c3e3)
- [Browser verification: approved continuation](https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/c9c19ae1783c43f8ec075f82a8c653a5?orgId=43303629-c7cb-4d5f-89c8-732d78cf1761&projectId=3fa20372-340e-40a3-bed9-841c1a90c3e3)

After 1's trace (`af34fd5b5156a22e441921fbf1db7602`) returned "Trace not found"
when checked through MCP. Its local SSE evidence survives, but do not use that
dashboard trace as proof. Fresh status checks are saved in
[northwind-trace-verification.json](northwind-trace-verification.json).

## Answer checks

Check the recommendation against the records, not just whether the run finishes:

| Fact | Source / calculation |
|---|---|
| Customer request $2,160; finance credit $720; incremental concession $1,440 | `finance/summary.md`; `customer-success/zendesk-export/tickets.csv`, ZD-10431 |
| Northwind $7,200 MRR / $86,400 ARR, 9% of current MRR | `finance/stripe-export/customers.csv`; $7,200 / $80,000 |
| Cash $6,019,000; Q3 average monthly net burn $295,061; runway about 20.4 months | `finance/summary.md`; cash / burn |
| Extra concession costs about 0.00488 months / 0.146 days of runway | $1,440 / $295,061; 30-day month, constant burn |
| Churn with no cost savings gives about 19.91 months of runway | $6,019,000 / ($295,061 + $7,200) |
| Notice deadline 16 Oct; renewal 15 Dec 2026 | `legal/contracts-register.csv`, CT-C-001 |
| Failed invoice $7,200, four attempts, next retry 14 Oct | `finance/stripe-export/failed-payments.csv`, FP-2001 |
| Two open P1 ingestion tickets | `customer-success/zendesk-export/tickets.csv`, ZD-10482 and ZD-10497 |

All three after answers retained the core $720 / $2,160 / $1,440 and
$7,200 / $86,400 figures. After 1 and After 2 also included the approximately
19.9-month no-savings churn case. After 3 used a gross-margin-adjusted estimate
of about 20.1 months instead and omitted the exact renewal date. It also asserted
an unsupported ~$540k increase in the fundraising milestone gap: losing $86,400
ARR widens that ARR gap by $86,400, all else equal. Do not present that answer as
fully verified. Legal conclusions also require the signed agreement and a full
uptime history; a missing record does not prove that termination is invalid.

The demo should show a recommendation with explicit assumptions, source paths,
and unresolved facts. It must not claim that a real credit was issued or that
live cfo.ai data was retrieved in this local-data scenario.

## Persistence bug found during browser verification

A capped run can have no assistant text at all. Mastra drops a saved message with
empty `parts`, which also loses its escalation metadata. The fix stores a short
budget-stop explanation when no partial text exists, so the pending offer remains
available after reload.

![Pending budget extension after a reload](evidence/2026-10-12/01-northwind-budget-extension-pending-desktop.png)

The empty-reply regression was reproduced with the Northwind question plus
"Do not send progress updates; respond only when the final recommendation is
ready." After the fix, reloading shows the fallback text and the pending card.
The same card was checked at 390 x 844 before clicking Deny.

![Empty-reply budget card on mobile](evidence/2026-10-12/02-northwind-empty-reply-reload-mobile.png)

## Fresh browser verification

The completed browser runs are recorded in
[northwind-browser-verification.json](northwind-browser-verification.json).

| Path | Initial capped cost | Continuation cost | Continuation steps | Outcome |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Approve | $0.020240 | $0.031799 | 10 | Completed within the $0.04 extension |
| Deny (empty-reply regression) | $0.026182 | $0.003093 | 1 | Tool-free answer marked Incomplete |

The repeated decision returned HTTP 409. Saved caps remained $0.02 during the
continuation and were reset to $0.25 / 300,000 afterwards. The usage panel now
shows the actual continuation budget ($0.04 approved, $0.01 denial backstop),
while the editor continues to edit the saved per-message caps.

The approved answer retained the core source figures and no-savings churn
calculation, but included errors in secondary reasoning: it called November
2026 after the December renewal, and overstated the incremental credit's
runway effect as 1.5 days. The $1,440 increment at $302,261 monthly burn is about
0.143 days. These are answer-quality limitations, not evidence that a credit was
issued. Verify the full answer before using it as a decision memo.

![Denied extension and incomplete answer](evidence/2026-10-12/04-northwind-incomplete-answer-desktop.png)

## Submission narrative

Open with the Northwind decision and the live cap/Approve recovery. Then show the
incident in Neatlogs, the repeated reads that motivated the fix, the prompt diff,
and the measured comparison. Explain Entire's coding checkpoints. Demonstrate
cfo.ai's actual contribution separately using the business plan or connected
workspace that you really used; this Northwind run alone does not demonstrate it.

content.text:
Here's what actually happened. To be upfront: **the app didn't find this by itself.** The agent I ran during Sprints 2 and 3 found it by reading the traces. Then we changed the bots' instructions.

## 1. How it was found
- The agent ran the Northwind question with a small cap and pulled the **neatlogs traces** for those runs, plus the app's own record of each step.
- Each trace lists every step: which bot ran, which tool it called, which file it read, and how many tokens that cost.
- The pattern was clear:
  - the **Primary Bot** read the company files, such as `finance/summary.md` and the customer and ticket files;
  - it passed the task to the **CFO Bot**;
  - the CFO Bot then **read the same 13–16 files again** (about 50 KB) and wrote a long report in one final step;
  - that final step is where the cap was crossed.
- Even with the normal limit, one of the 3 "before" runs ran out of its 300k-token budget for the same reason.

## 2. What was fixed
It's an instructions change, not new code (commit `8887e9ba`, `src/mastra/prompts/index.ts`):
- **Primary Bot:** when it hands a task to a specialist, it now quotes the figures it has already read, with their file paths.
- **Specialists** (CFO, Legal, Sales and the others): use the facts in the brief, don't reread those files, only read what's missing, and reply with a short summary of about 300 words instead of a full report.

## 3. Where the numbers come from
The agent ran the same Northwind question **3 times before and 3 times after** the change, with the normal limits, and counted from the logs:
- **CFO file reads:** 7 + 10 + 12 = **29** before, and 4 + 0 + 6 = **10** after.
- **Finished within the limit:** before, 2 of 3 runs finished (one hit the token limit); after, all 3 did.
- **CFO reply length:** about 26k characters → 6.7k.

## Caveats to state honestly
- Only 3 runs each, a small sample. Total cost fell only 3.3%, and the runs weren't faster.
- The **Neat Bot** didn't make the discovery. For the demo you can ask it to compare the two traces (the prompt with the trace IDs is in the demo doc). That shows neatlogs could have pointed to the problem, but don't claim the app found and fixed it on its own.

**How to put it in the demo:** *"neatlogs traces showed the CFO Bot rereading files the Primary Bot already had, and that's where the budget went. We changed the hand-off so specialists reuse those facts. CFO file reads dropped from 29 to 10, and all runs finished within budget."*

content.text:
Yes, this is good evidence, and in one way better than what we had: **the Neat Bot produced it live, from neatlogs data.** It also exposed two gaps you should know about.

## What it proves well ✅
- **Before vs after from neatlogs itself**, same question word for word:
  - status: error → success;
  - cost: $0.059 → $0.050 (−15%);
  - tokens: 324k → 237k (−27%);
  - the **"Execution Failed" detection** in the before run is gone in the after run.
- **It found the cause** from the trace contents:
  - **before:** the brief told the CFO Bot to "use the finance exports", it didn't pass the figures, and the CFO listed 10 files used;
  - **after:** the brief says "figures already read, no need to re-read", and the CFO replies in about 300 words.
- **It saw the prompt change** in the recorded inputs.
- It's careful: it says what the traces show and what they don't. Judges like that.

This covers Chetan's **"traces that drive decisions"** and **"before and after with numbers"** for this pair of runs. Screenshot all three parts.

## The two gaps it revealed ⚠️
1. **neatlogs records no tool calls.** It says "tool_calls: 0, no tool spans at all". So the "29 → 10 file reads" figure came from the app's own logs, not from neatlogs. neatlogs only has the bots' self-reports ("Files used…"), which it rightly calls "model text, not tool evidence".
2. **It misread why the before run failed.** It blamed the Sales Bot "dying" (6.4 ms, no LLM calls). That was actually the **cap**: once the budget ran out, the cap blocked the Sales Bot from starting. The Neat Bot couldn't tell because our cap details (the event and the attributes) aren't returned to it by the neatlogs tools. It did hedge ("consistent with, but not proof of").

## Is it enough?
**For the demo, yes:** show it as "the Neat Bot compares the traces and explains the fix". If you mention it, say the 29 → 10 file-read count comes from app logs and the cost and token numbers come from neatlogs.

**To make it airtight**, two small code changes would help:
- **Record tool calls in neatlogs**, such as `company_read_file` with the file path. The Neat Bot could then count the rereads itself.
- **Put the cap reason somewhere neatlogs returns**, such as a log line or the run's output text ("stopped: cost cap $0.02, tripped by CFO Bot"). It would then say "capped", not "Sales Bot died".

After that you'd rerun one before/after pair and ask the Neat Bot the same question. Should I make those two changes?

1. **Give it only the before trace.** If it sees the after trace, it's just reading the answer. Start a new Neat Bot chat with no mention of the fix.
2. **Don't present it as how we originally found the problem.** The chat timestamp will be after the fix commit, and a judge could notice. Present it as: *"the Neat Bot, given only the failed trace, independently suggests the same fix we made."* That claim holds up, and it's strong if its suggestion matches.

## Prompt for the new thread
> Trace 0ce0e491e0e1bdc3cf89d00ca4dfb65d failed. Diagnose it: why did it fail, where did the cost and tokens go (by agent and LLM call), and what in the delegation briefs or agent behaviour looks wasteful? Then suggest the 2–3 most effective changes to make this run cheaper and finish within budget, ranked by expected impact. Only use what the trace shows, and say what you can't see.

## What to expect
- **Good outcome:** it notices the CFO brief gives file paths but no figures, and the large CFO output with its 10-file list. It suggests "pass the figures in the brief" and "make specialists reply concisely". That's essentially our fix, so it's a strong piece of evidence.
- **Likely side point:** it may again blame the Sales Bot or suggest "fix the delegation failure", because it can't see the cap reason. That's fine. Its suggestion to cut tokens is still the right one, and the cap tripping on the Sales Bot's turn is what that failure was.
- **If it suggests something different,** don't use it as evidence. Keep the comparison chat on its own.

## Final evidence order
1. **Diagnosis:** the Neat Bot on the before trace only, with its suggested fixes (new thread).
2. **The fix:** the prompt diff (commit `8887e9ba`) and its Entire checkpoint.
3. **Verify:** the before-vs-after comparison you just ran.
4. The 3+3 run table from the demo doc, noting that the file-read counts come from app logs.

Send me the screenshots after you run it. I'll check whether its suggestion matches our fix closely enough to use, then put all of it into the evidence folder in that order.

- Select **Primary Bot**, then click the **bot name ▾** at the top and open the limits/usage panel.
- Set the **cost cap to `0.02`**. Leave the token cap at **300000**. Save.

## 3. Approve run
- Start a **new chat** with the Primary Bot and paste:

- Set the Primary Bot's caps back to **$0.25 / 300000** (or reset to default).

That's not an error. The panel shows two different things:

If neatlogs is still processing, the panel shows "not available yet" (`web/src/shell/UsagePanel.tsx:106-111`). Large, long runs like Northwind take neatlogs longer to process, so this is common.

So the trace is there. neatlogs just hadn't finished processing it when the app checked. Open the link in a minute or two and it should all show.
